subject: Request: pause auto-renew for pilot + TFC conditioning and 45/90 notice sync
messages:
From: Laura Chan <laura.chan@stellarhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@stellarhealth.com, pranav.singh@stellarhealth.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot contracting: ask about auto-renew and termination carve 

Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal here (copied) asked a couple quick questions about the MSA wording for pilots: specifically whether the auto-renew clause can be paused during an initial pilot period, and whether we can limit "Termination for Convenience" (TFC) carve-in so that pilot customers have an expedited off-ramp without the usual notice windows.

High level ask: can Redwood provide a short-term carve (3 months) that suspends auto-renew and allows StellarHealth to exit without an early-exit fee during pilot adequacy testing? They prefer a 45-day notice but are open to 60 or staged 45/90 depending on onboarding milestones.

Attached is a draft redline from our side (pilot scope SOW included). Can your team confirm what you can accept and what needs legal review?

Appreciate it — Laura

--
Laura Chan
Head of Vendor Ops | StellarHealth
laura.chan@stellarhealth.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chan <laura.chan@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, contracts@stellarhealth.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot contracting: ask about auto-renew and termination carve 

Laura —

Thanks for sending the redline and SOW. Short answer: yes, we can accommodate a pilot-specific off-ramp, but there are a couple of options and trade-offs to be explicit about. 

Proposals we can consider now (quick summary):
- Option A (preferred for both sides): Temporary auto-renew suspension for the pilot term only (explicitly stated in Order Form), with a 45-day notice to avoid auto-renew starting the Production term. TFC during pilot permitted without fee.
- Option B: 60-day notice for both pilot exit and production; TFC allowed in pilot but requires short ramp-down support fee (prorated).
- Option C: Staggered notice: 45 days for pilot exit within the first 90 days; reverts to standard 90-day production notice afterward.

Operationally we need explicit handoff criteria in the SOW that mark the pilot as "pilot concluded" (e.g., evaluation metrics, data export trigger) so our billing and provisioning teams can stop the automatic renewal. Without that signal, our system assumes standard auto-renew cadence.

I'm looping in Karthik and Stephanie from Sales/Legal ops to coordinate the formal redline and a short legal review. Ben from Finance is cc'd to confirm whether a ramp-down fee (Option B) is acceptable commercially.

Next steps: Karthik/Stephanie — can you review the attached redline and propose language for Option A vs Option C? If Legal needs to mark up the MSA, we'll run a quick SOW amendment that explicitly suspends Section 4.2 (Auto-Renew) during the pilot.

Laura — can you confirm the pilot start date and the desired pilot length so we can map the notice windows to calendar dates?

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Laura Chan <laura.chan@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, contracts@stellarhealth.com
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 10:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot contracting: ask about auto-renew and termination carve 

Folks —

Quick read of Stellar's redline attached. I like Marissa's Option A but want to add a short gating paragraph that ties the suspension to two things: (1) the SOW test criteria are met AND (2) Stellar has completed onboarding data export/testing. Proposed clause (draft language):

"During the Pilot Term defined in the Order Form, Section 4.2 (Auto-Renew) shall be suspended. If Customer elects not to transition to a Production Order Form at the end of the Pilot Term, Customer may terminate for convenience effective upon thirty (30) days' written notice provided the Pilot Handoff Criteria in the attached SOW have been met; otherwise, standard notice periods apply."

Rationale: 30 days gives us time to quiesce traffic and run a clean KV cache flush; it's also less friction for pilots. If Stellar insists on 45, we can accept. Stephanie — can Legal review that clause and advise if "Pilot Handoff Criteria" is legally specific enough or if we need to enumerate the criteria in the MSA itself? Ben — is Finance ok with 0 fee on pilot TFC if handoff criteria are met?

Laura — we understand pilots are expected to run 75 days starting 2027-05-03 per your note in the SOW. Confirm if that's accurate.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Laura Chan <laura.chan@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, contracts@stellarhealth.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot contracting: ask about auto-renew and termination carve 

All —

Legal reviewed Karthik's proposed language. We're comfortable with the overall approach but recommend two clarifications before we exchange final redlines:

1) Define "Pilot Handoff Criteria" in the SOW (explicit bullet list): a) export of test dataset; b) completion of acceptance test checklist in Appendix A; c) written confirmation from Customer PM. This avoids ambiguity.

2) Change the proposed 30-day termination effective date to 45 days for balance of operational risk unless Stellar confirms they can provide the written confirmation 45 days prior to desired TFC effective date. We can add a carve that allows a 30-day effective date if Redwood's Oncall certifies low-impact shutdown (rare).

Suggested final MSA snippet:

"During the Pilot Term set forth in the applicable Order Form, Section 4.2 (Auto-Renew) shall be suspended solely for the Pilot Term. If Customer elects to not transition to Production, Customer may terminate for convenience upon forty-five (45) days' prior written notice provided the Pilot Handoff Criteria (defined in the attached SOW) have been satisfied. Notwithstanding the foregoing, where Redwood's operations team certifies in writing that shutdown impact is minimal, the Parties may agree to a thirty (30)-day termination effective date.

Legal is happy to mark this into an MSA amendment. Once Stellar confirms pilot dates and SOW acceptance we will produce the redline.

Laura — can you confirm pilot start (proposed 2027-05-03) and whether Stellar is okay with the SOW kule (PM sign-off + acceptance checklist)?

Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: 20270405_StellarHealth_MSA_redline_v1.docx; pilot_scope_SOW_v2.pdf
"
